analysis:
This PR contains only documentation and a changelog entry: changelog.d/provider-prompt-token-reuse.md, docs/architecture/components/provider.md (head lines 76-83) and docs/architecture/inference.md (patch hunk at head lines 1030-1046). No source code was supplied, so the behavior these docs describe could not be verified.

Described changes and the security-relevant questions each raises:
1. A prompt token-ID cache (PromptTokenCache) reuses tokens per prefix-cache scope. This is in-memory plaintext-derived state on the T-041 / TB-007 boundary. The docs say reuse never crosses a cache scope and that the scope is the coordinator-authored cacheSalt. A request that is not cache-scoped or has caching disabled must not read or publish entries. Cross-account leakage here would only matter if the scoping were not implemented as documented. Preparation-time differences between hits and misses (5-8 ms versus 100+ ms) add a timing signal alongside the existing accepted SEC-035 TTFT oracle. It stays within the same-scope boundary if scoping holds, so T-041 may need an update noting the token-cache channel. The cache has no stated TTL or size bound, and it must not persist to disk. DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0 is the kill switch.
2. The cold-load work-consumer release (ProviderLoop+WorkFIFO.swift) removes head-of-line blocking. Cancels are applied when admission returns, so a cancel for a waiting request could race with its start of inference. Ordering relative to the connection-invalidation and grant-revocation paths (T-053, TB-011) should be checked. The docs say connection, drain and model-management events still wait for the load. A request admitted before a grant revocation or reconnect must not begin inference after it. Concurrency also raises GPU and memory pressure with several models loading (T-029).
3. Linear-time Gemma 4 and GPT-OSS template rewrites (ChatTemplateLoopRewrites) carry correctness risk. The docs state a load-time check and sampled comparisons against the served template, with reuse disabled on mismatch.
4. DARKBLOOM_TTFT_* env knobs are described. Whether they are in passthroughEnvKeys is unverified. They only disable optimizations.

No concrete regression is shown by the supplied evidence, and I did not verify that the scoping, cancel ordering or rewrite checks are implemented. Deeper review of the Swift source is warranted.
